viewer.scope: Four fresh isolated sessions; three representative TTKN originals and one previously validated unencrypted positive PDF. No UI clicks or credentials supplied. All four final full frames visually inspected; 20/25-second frames stable. Other 13 TTKN originals NOT_RUN. Error text is not legible in the available viewer font environment, so no error cause is inferred. Offline failure is not irrecoverability proof, and #441 remains open.

research_limits.not_standard_pkcs7_recipients: All 16 contain the same eight-byte AppendCA marker instead of a PKCS#7 recipient envelope
research_limits.not_standard_pkcs12_on_single_base64_dec: All 14 opaque PFX fields fail ASN.1 structural parsing before meaningful password verification
research_limits.password_lengths: The 14 embedded-certificate wrappers decode password to 128 bytes; the two server wrappers decode it to 48 bytes. Length does not prove an algorithm or plaintext credential.
research_limits.no_external_authentication: No embedded endpoint was contacted and no password search was run
research_limits.no_exception_claim: Missing semantics and credentials remain research questions; neither parser refusal nor offline viewer failure proves unavoidable loss.

primary_sources.use: Standard security-handler selection, recipient/private-key model and crypt filters; does not specify TTKN.PubSec.s1
PFX ASN.1 outer structure; a field name alone does not establish PKCS#12 encoding

initial_attempts.detail: An initial fixed CRLF assumption at the trailer and incomplete XML tag allowlist were corrected to measured line offsets and the server tag; all sources were rerun after correction. No source was changed.
Retained historical probe must not establish empty-password availability or successful decryption; the actual live dictionary is the TTKN profile inventoried here.

public_signature_hypothesis_probe.scope: Offline public-key-only test of whether the password field is a PKCS#1 v1.5 signature block under the embedded public certificate. No private operation, password search, value export or decryption claim.
